The Heat have retired six numbers, although only five of the players played for the franchise. Michael Jordan was the first player to be honored despite not having played for the Heat. Pat Riley retired Jordan's signature No. 23 before his final game in Miami during the 2002–03 season as a tribute to his career.[54]


During the 2005–06 season the organization honored Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Dan Marino's No. 13 in respect of his contributions to the National Football League (NFL)'s Miami Dolphins.[55] However, the No. 13 jersey is not retired and is still available for use by the Heat players.


The NBA retired Bill Russell's No. 6 for all its member teams on August 11, 2022.[56][57]

On June 2, 2017, the NBA ruled that Bosh's blood clotting issues were a career-ending illness, meaning the Heat would be allowed to remove his contract from their salary cap once they officially released him.[4] Two days later, the Heat announced that they had waived Bosh, ending a seven-year stint with the organization.[107] Following Bosh's release, Heat President Pat Riley said, "The number '1' will never be worn by another player and we can't wait to someday hang his jersey in the rafters".[108] In February 2018, Bosh declared himself on the comeback trail, having refused to rule out a return to the NBA.[6][109]


On February 12, 2019, Bosh announced that he was no longer pursuing his NBA career[110] and that he planned to retire from the NBA when his jersey was retired by the Heat.[111] The Heat retired Bosh's No. 1 jersey on March 26 before a regular season game against the Orlando Magic.[8][9]
